test_title: PYST 03: SSC Stenographer 2025: English Language & Comprehension (Held On: 06 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Arrange the sentence parts:

(A) after the meeting

(B) the team members

(C) went

(D) to a restaurant
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4** i.e. **BACD**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence begins with the subject **"the team members"**, correctly indicated by **part (B)**.
 
• The time phrase **"after the meeting"** (**part A**) is placed immediately after the subject to indicate when the action occurred.
 
• The verb **"went"** (**part C**) follows the subject and time phrase to show the action.
 
• The prepositional phrase **"to a restaurant"** (**part D**) indicates the destination, completing the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **BACD.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (ABCD):** Incorrect because starting with "after the meeting" before the subject makes the sentence incomplete and awkward.
 
• **Option 2 (BADC):** Incorrect because placing the destination "to a restaurant" before the verb "went" disrupts natural sentence flow.
 
• **Option 3 (BCAD):** Incorrect because putting "after the meeting" after the verb "went" changes the standard placement of time phrases in English sentences.
